name: Laha (Indonesia)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only Collins 1983 comparative-historical classification of Central Maluku; no phonological description found

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1983. The historical relationships of the languages of Central Maluku, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics D-47. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Only a West Piru Bay statement (p.82): 'Stress in Hoamoal languages is always penultimate; if a suffix or particle is added to the word the stress shifts accordingly. In Asilulu this is not the case. The stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the root word'. Laha (East Piru Bay > Ambon subgroup) appears only in reflex tables and classification; no Laha stress statement anywhere (all 'stress'/'penult' hits checked).

sources.citation: Badan Bahasa, Peta Bahasa (petabahasa.kemendikdasmen.go.id), Provinsi Maluku language list
sources.note: No entry for Laha among the 62 Maluku languages listed.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste. Language Science Press (langsci 526).
sources.note: Nothing for Laha: Laha [lhh] appears only in the Solehua > Seram Straits > Ambon > Central Ambon classification (sister of Seit-Kaitetu) and in a note on genitive-system collapse citing Collins 1980.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 2022. Language death in Indonesia: a sociocultural pandemic. Linguistik Indonesia 40(2). doi:10.26499/li.v40i2.347
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that Collins (1980) 'published an essay about the Laha language.. Aspects of Laha grammar and phonology indicate that Laha is indeed a separate Central Maluku language related to the languages of Seit and Hitu' -- i.e. confirms Collins 1980 is the primary description containing phonology.

sources.citation: Travis, Edgar W. 1989. A lexicostatistic survey of the languages indigenous to Ambon Island. In W. D. Laidig (ed.), Maluku (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 6), 64-102. Ambon: UNPATTI & SIL.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.3.2: 'The Laha language is spoken by part of the residents of the village of Laha, located near Ambon's commercial airport on the north shore of the outer bay. Laha has only one dialect.' Lexicostatistics and demography only; no occurrence of stress/accent/penult.
